findings.issue: The formation-free-energy formula omits stoichiometric coefficients. Write ΔG°ᵣₓₙ = Σ nΔG°f(products) − Σ nΔG°f(reactants), with n defined as the balanced-equation coefficient.
findings.evidence: Standard free energies of formation are molar quantities, so each must be multiplied by the corresponding stoichiometric coefficient. This is a standard-chemistry clarification of the source's shorthand summation notation; the draft otherwise risks teaching an incorrect calculation whenever a coefficient is not 1.

findings.issue: Qualify the favorability criterion as applying under standard-state conditions. As written, it can imply that ΔG° determines the direction of a process under any conditions.
findings.evidence: The source and CED explicitly restrict ΔG° to standard states. As a matter of standard chemistry, ΔG determines favorability at the actual composition, whereas ΔG° < 0 establishes favorability under standard-state conditions and corresponds to K > 1.
